THE_LEADING_HYPOTHESIS_AND_IT_IS_NOT_CON.claim: Its reasoning may be discarded between turns, so it re-derives from scratch every decision and flails.
THE_LEADING_HYPOTHESIS_AND_IT_IS_NOT_CON.mechanism: The server ran with --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3, so vLLM splits thinking into reasoning_content. tool_agent.py:1037 READS that correctly (it falls back to reasoning_content). But line 2267 WRITES it back as assistant_message['reasoning']. If Nemotron's chat template renders reasoning_content, as the vLLM convention implies and as Flash-Next's template provably does (the GG5 defect), the thinking is dropped on the way back in.
THE_LEADING_HYPOTHESIS_AND_IT_IS_NOT_CON.consistency: It fits the shape: more actions, similar per-action effort, no accumulation. An agent with no memory of why it acted would act more and learn less.
THE_LEADING_HYPOTHESIS_AND_IT_IS_NOT_CON.WHY_IT_IS_NOT_CONFIRMED: I do not have Nemotron's chat_template.jinja locally and have not verified that it reads reasoning_content rather than reasoning. Calling this proven would repeat the two mistakes I already made today. It is a hypothesis with a precedent in this exact codebase.
THE_LEADING_HYPOTHESIS_AND_IT_IS_NOT_CON.the_cheap_decisive_test: Re-run with NO --reasoning-parser. The thinking then stays inline in `content`, which is carried verbatim, so nothing can be dropped. One flag, and it discriminates the hypothesis from 'the model is unsuited' in a single run.

WHAT_IS_SETTLED_REGARDLESS: Integration is not the obstacle and never was after the parser fix. Nemotron fits the card, loads in 92 s, serves at 44.36x concurrency against the incumbent's 5.99x measured on a matched control, and speaks our tool protocol unmodified. Whatever is wrong is above the wiring.
WHAT_THIS_DOES_NOT_LICENSE: It does not license 'Nemotron is a bad model'. It licenses 'Nemotron in THIS harness, with the reasoning parser active, scored 1 level'.
